pages.text: Dingding washed an apron. Water dripped. "Where to hang it?"
Dingding checked the bank soil. Dark on one side, pale and dry on the other.
Mom looked down from the upper field. "Sun shines well there. Hang it there."
"But it is damp, Mom." "Fine. I looked." Mom passed with a basket on her head.
She spread her own towel on the dark soil, then went upstairs.
Grandma opened the upper field. "Water coming!" Water trickled over the bank.
It ran only onto the dark soil. Mom's towel floated up. "My towel!"
Dingding went to the pale soil and spread the apron there.
A gentle breeze dried it, flutter, flutter.
Mom's towel floated to the lower field. A duck climbed onto it. "Mom! Your towel is a boat!"
